seo.description: Prepare an airport service provider's assessment: responsibilities, custody, subcontractors, contractual requirements, limits and unresolved questions.
seo.keywords: airport liability insurance Moldova, ground handling liability, airport service provider, property in custody airport, aviation liability assessment

content:
Airport liability starts with the services actually performed and the relationships between operators. Managing a terminal, ground handling, baggage handling and maintaining installations are not the same activity. A business working at an airport is not automatically protected by another entity's policy. For a company in the Republic of Moldova, assessment starts with its precise role and contractual documents.

A local insurer presents a category for airports and related services. That public information does not confirm acceptance of a particular provider or all its operations. This article prepares a risk assessment without promising an offer. Aeronautical requirements, authorizations, security and operational procedures require separate verification with competent authorities and specialists. The text establishes no technical standards and gives no instructions for working in airport areas.

A map of activities is the first useful document

List the company's services and where they are performed, at the level necessary for assessment. Distinguish premises management, handling and other contracted services. The broad label airport activity cannot replace this list. A proposal may describe one particular service rather than the whole airport and every business working there.

For each activity identify the provider and contractual customer. Where subcontractors are involved, explain their role without assuming automatic transfer of liability. A service agreement and an insurance policy are different documents. Obligations towards the customer require legal review and comparison with the protection actually accepted, not an assumption that all contractual duties are insured.

Distinguish your property from other people's property

A business may own equipment while temporarily handling customers' property. Damage to its own equipment and liability for property in its care raise different questions. Identify the type of property, owner and service stage at which it is received. Custody is not a category automatically included in every liability policy.

Describe baggage, cargo or aircraft relationships precisely. Do not publish passenger data, property identifiers or commercially sensitive information in a general request. Initial discussion can use categories and aggregate values. Detailed documents should follow an agreed channel after clarifying why they are needed and who will review them.

Who is insured, and in what capacity?

Check the exact company name, relevant branches and accepted activity in the proposed document. Membership of the same group or participation in one contract does not mean automatic inclusion. Ask how employees, collaborators and subcontractors are treated rather than assuming these categories occupy identical contractual positions.

If the customer requests that it be named in a document, have appropriate specialists review the wording and its effect. Do not copy a clause from a foreign contract and present it as automatically applicable in Moldova. Retain the original requirement and exact response. An unclear expression should remain an open question, not a completed compliance check.

Describe claims in separate categories

Prepare separate questions about bodily injury, property damage and defence costs where relevant. Do not assume all are accepted in every form. A claim can involve a person, an asset and a complex contractual relationship. Determining liability requires examination of facts, contracts and the applicable framework.

Identify financial consequences without physical damage separately. A service delay or commercial penalty must not automatically be added to the meaning of insured damage. Request review without promising compensation for every effect of operational disruption. If the proposal does not answer a question, mark that component unconfirmed.

The relationship with aircraft insurance

An aircraft owner's or operator's policy and a ground provider's liability cover serve different interests. The first does not establish protection for the provider's service. Equally, the provider's document is not a replacement for aircraft insurance. For a new contract request review of the relationships and its specific requirements.

The Civil Aviation Authority publishes information about insurance in air transport. Concrete obligations, compulsory limits and operating requirements need specialist verification at the decision date. This article sets none of those limits and does not interpret international regimes. A general answer about an insurance category cannot establish compliance with a particular project or agreement.

Locations and changes in services

Describe relevant locations without publishing sensitive plans, access areas or security procedures. A provider may work in several spaces or add a service. Request review before treating an existing policy as sufficient. The same customer and team do not necessarily mean the declared activity remains unchanged.

Keep a version record showing the original service, proposed change, communication date and response. Overseas work requires its own review. Policy territory and authorization to operate are different matters. This article does not recommend changing technical procedures to fit insurance wording.

Information useful for assessing exposure

Prepare service descriptions and indicators requested by the evaluator with a clear period and calculation basis. Do not invent volumes to complete a form. Mark unavailable information and identify the internal source able to confirm it. Activity data should be traceable to company documents rather than a verbal estimate alone.

Communicate incidents and complaints fully through a confidential channel. Do not publish personal details or litigation documents. An already known event requires separate review of the chronology and potentially relevant policies. A proposal for a future period must not be described as an automatic solution to an existing claim.

Limits, deductibles and defence costs

A limit is a relevant contractual ceiling, not a promise to pay every complaint. Check whether the document distinguishes an event, certain categories and the whole period. Ask how defence costs are treated and whether they affect available limits. Answers must refer to the actual proposed conditions, not assumptions drawn from another product.

The deductible is the part of a loss borne under the contract. Read how it applies and the exclusions, meaning situations without cover. Compare the premium, the price of insurance, only after aligning services, periods and limits. A lower price for a narrower activity is not automatically the same protection at a better cost.

Example: a provider expands its contract

In a hypothetical scenario, a terminal service provider receives an additional task involving the customer's property. Before relying on the old policy, it identifies the new service, custody relationship and contractual obligations. This example is not a real operation or ING Broker customer and confirms no project's eligibility.

The company prepares separate questions for its own equipment, property received and claims from others. It communicates the change before telling the customer that the insurance requirement is met. Where there is no clear confirmation, the point remains open. This administrative approach neither authorizes the operation nor replaces technical or security checks.

How to keep a usable file

The file can contain an entity sheet, service map, contractual requirements and insurance documents, each with a version and date. Keep sensitive annexes separately. Responsible staff should see what was proposed, accepted and left unresolved without reconstructing an unordered email archive.

The broker can help structure and compare information within its mandate. It does not establish airport procedures or assume the insurer's role in examining compensation. Before communicating with a customer, check that the insurance statement corresponds to the document actually issued. Advice or discussion must not be presented as an effective policy.

The provider's preparation checklist

  • Relevant entities, roles and subcontractors.
  • Actual services, locations and operating periods.
  • Owned property and property temporarily in custody.
  • Contracts and insurance requirements requiring review.
  • Verified indicators and confidential incident history.
  • Project changes and unanswered questions.
  • The issued document, conditions and confirmations kept together.

What information can be lost between providers?

In a chain of services, uncertainty may arise precisely when property or a task passes from one business to another. Describe the stages and handover records without operational or security details. Assessment needs to show where the company's contractual service starts and ends, not merely where an asset happens to stand.

Do not invent a retrospective boundary to fit a proposal. If two documents describe the same stage differently, seek legal and commercial clarification before making a statement to the customer. Insurance does not automatically resolve inconsistent provider agreements. The evaluator needs the actual relationship, not a simplified version chosen for a lower price.

At renewal keep a list of services added, removed or subcontracted differently. An unchanged equipment inventory does not prove unchanged contractual exposure. This record supports precise questions and does not replace authorized airport or provider procedures.

For an administrative example, a task description may say that one company receives property, while the service annex refers to another contractor. The file should retain both descriptions and the question needing clarification. An insurance certificate bearing a familiar company name cannot reconcile this discrepancy. The responsible commercial and legal contacts need to identify the actual contracting parties before the statement is treated as settled.

Similarly, separate historical activity indicators from forecasts. If a future contract changes the scope, label the new figures as a proposal supported by that contract, not as completed work. A period, unit and source beside each indicator make differences visible. This does not establish an acceptable risk level or a premium; it simply gives the evaluator a consistent basis for questions.

Frequently asked questions about airport liability

Does the airport's policy automatically include every provider?

No. Check the entities and activities in the actual document. Presence at a location does not establish inclusion in its owner's or operator's policy.

Is aircraft insurance enough for a service company?

Do not assume so. The aircraft and the provider's liability represent different interests. Review the contractual relationship and actual service separately.

Are commercial penalties automatically insured?

No. Identify the obligation and request review of the terms. A payment in a commercial agreement does not automatically become compensation due under insurance.

Can we add a service without updating the file?

Do not assume the change has no effect. Describe the new activity and request review before presenting protection as unchanged. Technical requirements and authorizations remain separate.

Risk acceptance, conditions and claims settlement belong to the insurer under the contract. This guide confirms neither product availability nor cover for a particular case.
